ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of the foreign corporate investor, all direct and ultimate shareholders, the proposed legal representative, and counterparties against: (i) domestic, foreign and international-organization politically exposed persons (PEPs) as defined in Article 3 of Law No. 14/2022/QH15; (ii) the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions lists and the Al-Qaida/ISIL sanctions lists; (iii) the State Bank of Viet Nam's terrorism and weapons-of-mass-destruction proliferation financing watchlists; (iv) OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists; and (v) domestic regulatory enforcement and red-flag lists. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is mandatory for PEPs and high-risk jurisdictions in accordance with Circular No. 09/2023/TT-NHNN. For the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML risk tier applicable to this M&A advisory boutique, a written UBO-piercing analysis and sanctions/PEP screening evidence must be maintained in the pre-incorporation due diligence pack and submitted with the Investment Registration Certificate dossier.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Business Registration Portal (Cổng thông tin quốc gia về đăng ký doanh nghiệp) – https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn; processed by the Business Registration Office of the provincial-level Department of Planning and Investment
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Articles 38-40 of Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 and Articles 15-17 of Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP, the official enterprise name must be denominated in the Vietnamese language using Latin-script Vietnamese characters, and may include Arabic numerals and the symbols '&', '.', '+', '-'. The name must contain at least two elements: the legal form descriptor (e.g., 'Công ty TNHH') and the distinctive proper name. A parallel name in a foreign language may be registered in addition, and a transliteration in Roman script is acceptable, provided the distinctive element contains at least one letter, is not composed solely of numbers or symbols, and is not identical or confusingly similar to any existing protected enterprise name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Tokens identical or confusingly similar to the name of any existing registered enterprise whose name is legally protected (e.g., names differing only by a diacritic mark, word order, symbol, legal form suffix, or containing a distinctive element that is already protected)
Tokens that violate Vietnamese historical, cultural, ethical and customary traditions, including disrespectful references to national heroes, political figures, or national heritage

Tokens identical or confusingly similar to the name of a State administrative agency, People's armed forces unit, political organization, or socio-political-professional organization (e.g., 'Chính phủ', 'Bộ', 'Uỷ ban nhân dân', 'Tổng cục', 'Quốc hội', 'Vietnam' used alone in a way that implies State affiliation) without prior written consent of the competent agency

Tokens implying a regulated financial activity without the appropriate license: 'Bank', 'Ngân hàng', 'Insurance', 'Bảo hiểm', 'Securities', 'Chứng khoán', 'Investment Fund', 'Quỹ đầu tư', 'Finance', 'Brokerage', which require prior licensing by the State Bank of Viet Nam or the State Securities Commission; a pure M&A advisory boutique may not use these tokens in its Vietnamese enterprise name unless it holds the corresponding regulatory license

Official names and emblems of foreign states, international organizations, or diplomatic missions when used without authorization, and any token likely to mislead the public as to the enterprise's legal status, industry, or governmental affiliation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Viet Nam does not operate a standalone name-reservation or extension mechanism. The proposed name is examined as part of the enterprise registration dossier, and the Business Registration Office must issue the Enterprise Registration Certificate or notify the applicant of necessary corrections within three (3) working days of submitting a complete and valid dossier, in accordance with Articles 26-27 of Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP. If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant receives a written notice stating the grounds (Article 28) and may: (i) revise the proposed name and resubmit an amended electronic dossier without additional State fee, with a new statutory review of three (3) working days; (ii) file a first-instance administrative complaint with the Director of the Department of Planning and Investment within ninety (90) days of receiving the rejection notice, in accordance with Law on Complaints No. 02/2011/QH13; and (iii) in the event the complaint is dismissed or not resolved to the applicant's satisfaction, initiate administrative court proceedings at the competent provincial People's Court under the Law on Administrative Procedures No. 93/2015/QH13 within the statutory limitation period. Pre-consultation with the Business Registration Office through the National Portal is strongly recommended where sensitive or industry-specific tokens are contemplated.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office (address-only premise without a lease or right-of-use in the name of the company) is not acceptable as the registered address under Article 43 of Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 and Article 27 of Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP. The registered office must be a definite address in Viet Nam evidenced by a written lease, sub-lease, or ownership document showing lawful use by the enterprise. A serviced or co-working office lease executed in the company's name is accepted. A home-office address may be accepted only where the premises are legally usable for the registered business purpose and the requisite supporting documents are provided.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium: approximately 30-40% likelihood of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 24 months of registration, driven by (i) authorities' post-issuance verification campaigns on registered address authenticity, (ii) elevated scrutiny of multiple companies registered at the same address, and (iii) the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML/CFT risk tier applicable to M&A advisory firms. Registration at condominium or shared residential addresses increases the likelihood materially.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 (effective 1 January 2021), in particular Articles 26, 27, 34, 46-79 and 75-76 applicable to limited liability companies, Article 74 on legal representation, and Chapter VII on enterprise registration; Law on Investment No. 61/2020/QH14, Articles 38-39 and the negative list as implemented by Decree No. 31/2021/ND-CP; Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP on Enterprise Registration, Forms II.1 and II.2; Circular No. 47/2019/TT-BTC on registration fees (online filing exempt); Law on Securities No. 54/2019/QH14 and Decree No. 86/2016/ND-CP (secondary applicability where securities-linked M&A advice is rendered); Law on Anti-Money Laundering No. 04/2024/QH15 (effective 1 July 2025); Law on Occupational Safety and Health No. 84/2015/QH13; Law on Environmental Protection No. 72/2020/QH14 and Decree No. 08/2022/ND-CP.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Business Registration Office, provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, operating the National Business Registration Portal (dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn) under the Ministry of Planning and Investment; foreign-investment approval is equally centralized before the same DPI through the National Investment Registration System. The statutory filing fee is effectively USD 0.00 because online enterprise registration is free of charge; nominal paper-dossier notarization and gazette-publication costs are payable to third-party notary offices and the national portal operator.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Investment Registration (Form A.1 per Decree No. 31/2021/ND-CP) resulting in the Investment Registration Certificate (Giay chung nhan dang ky dau tu); Application for Enterprise Registration (Form II.1 per Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP) resulting in the Certificate of Enterprise Registration (Giay chung nhan dang ky doanh nghiep), which issues simultaneously the Enterprise Code and Tax Identification Number and constitutes the operating business license for non-conditional ISIC 7020 advisory services.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Viet Nam imposes no statutory minimum charter capital for a management-consultancy LLC under ISIC 7020; the foreign investor must nevertheless demonstrate financial capacity, and the charter capital must be reasonably proportional to the scale of the M&A advisory project. The registered charter capital must be fully contributed in cash within 90 days from the Certificate of Enterprise Registration, paid via an inward transfer into the Company's Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) opened at a licensed commercial bank. The DICA operates as a monitored capital escrow because subsequent foreign-currency inflows, including M&A success-fee wires, must be received through it and are subject to foreign-exchange and anti-money-laundering verification by the custodian bank.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 01/2025 OF THE MEMBERS' COUNCIL OF [FULL ENGLISH NAME] LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY (THE COMPANY), ADOPTED ON 7 JANUARY 2025 AT HANOI, SOCIALIST REPUBLIC OF VIET NAM. QUORUM: 100% OF THE FOUNDING MEMBERS DULY REPRESENTED. RESOLVED UNANIMOUSLY AS FOLLOWS: (1) Charter Capital Subscription: the initial charter capital of the Company is VND 5,000,000,000 (five billion Vietnamese Dong) or the equivalent in US Dollars, subscribed proportionally by the founding Members as set out in the Members' Register; the capital contributions shall be paid in full no later than 90 days from the Certificate of Enterprise Registration by wire transfer into the Company's Direct Investment Capital Account opened at a licensed commercial bank in Viet Nam. (2) Adoption of Constitutional Instruments: the Company Charter and the Internal Corporate Governance and AML Policy are adopted, and the General Director is authorized to file them with the Department of Planning and Investment. (3) Registered Office: the registered office is approved at [Suite No., Building Name, Street, Ward, District], Hanoi, Viet Nam, pursuant to the executed office lease and the lessor's notarized consent to the use of the premises as the Company's registered address. (4) Officers and Legal Representation: [Full Name of Appointee] is appointed General Director and sole Legal Representative of the Company; [Full Name of Appointee] is appointed Chief Financial Officer; [Full Name of Appointee] is appointed AML Compliance Officer charged with the Law on Anti-Money Laundering No. 04/2024/QH15 and shall be the named officer for suspicious-transaction reporting on success-fee payment rails. (5) Banking and Signatory Mandates: the Company shall open bank accounts, including the Direct Investment Capital Account, and the General Director together with the Chief Financial Officer are authorized as joint signatories. (6) Corporate Seal: the design and custody policy of the Company's corporate seal are approved, and the General Director is instructed to notify the seal imprint to the National Business Registration Portal. (7) Statutory Licensing and Market Access: the Company's business line is limited to middle-market cross-border cross-industry Mergers and Acquisitions advisory under ISIC 7020 / NAICS 523150; the Company shall not engage in deposit-taking, asset management, proprietary dealing, or providing securities advice to listed issuers without first obtaining the applicable State Securities Commission authorization. (8) Authorizations: all filings with the Department of Planning and Investment, taxation authorities, social-insurance agency, fire-prevention authority and environmental authority are approved and the competent officers are authorized to execute the same. This Resolution takes effect on adoption and supersedes all prior preliminary arrangements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, Notarization and Localization of Foundation Dossier; Registered Office Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Vietnamese notary offices under the provincial Department of Justice; Consular Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for post-legalization; landlord and building-management representative of the proposed registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the foreign investor's corporate authority documents (certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, board authorization to establish the Vietnamese LLC, passport copies of ultimate beneficial owners) and arrange certified Vietnamese translation and consular legalization or apostille. Execute the office lease agreement with the building owner or authorized sub-lessor, and obtain the lessor's notarized confirmation that the leased floor area is lawfully available for use as the Company's registered address. Conduct a preliminary name search on the National Business Registration Portal for the proposed English and Vietnamese names, and verify that the intended business scope in ISIC 7020 is outside the Decree 31/2021/ND-CP negative list. Retain all notarized exemplars in the dossier book for the IRC and CER filing steps.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney for the founding investor's signatory
Certified true copies of the investor's certificate of incorporation and good-standing
Certified true copies of the passport or identity documents of all ultimate beneficial owners
Notarized office lease agreement and landlord's consent letter
Draft Charter of the LLC in Vietnamese and English
Members' quota schedule reflecting the subscribed charter capital split
AML policy skeleton addressing M&A success-fee wire monitoring
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed company name is refused for similarity, promptly file a revised name request or an objection with the Business Registration Office; if a notary declines to certify due to defective authority, cure by obtaining a supplemental power-of-attorney or re-notarized translation; if the landlord's consent is deficient, secure a conforming, notarized replacement declaration from the building owner.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) Application and Negative-List Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) of the province of the registered office, acting through the National Investment Registration System single-window online portal (dautu.gov.vn)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Form A.1 Application for Investment Registration together with the project proposal describing the M&A advisory boutique's projected revenue model, principal lines of cross-border and cross-industry middle-market deal-making advisory, committed charter capital, proposed head-office address, and implementation timeline. As ISIC 7020 is not found on the negative list of Decree No. 31/2021/ND-CP, the application shall be processed in the standard 15-working-day window. The application must contain a compliance undertaking that the boutique will not conduct securities dealing, asset management, deposit-taking, or unlicensed securities advisory on listed securities. The DPI issues the Investment Registration Certificate containing the investment objective, project scale, location, charter capital, and investor identity.
required_dossiers: Form A.1 Application for Investment Registration
Dated project proposal with financial projections and headcount plan
Financial capacity evidence of the foreign investor (bank statement or audited financial statements)
Notarized office lease and landlord's consent
Certified and translated investor incorporation documents
Undertaking to open a Direct Investment Capital Account at a licensed Vietnamese bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DPI issues a written query or refusal, cure by submitting a supplemental or amended dossier within 14 days; if refusal is premised on an allegedly conditional sector, re-scope the ISIC 7020 description to pure advisory services and delete any language referencing securities dealing or fund management, then resubmit. A final contested refusal may be appealed to the Ministry of Planning and Investment or by administrative court action under the Law on Administrative Procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Enterprise Registration Certificate (CER) Filing and Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registration Office, Department of Planning and Investment, via the National Business Registration Portal (dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the National Business Registration Portal and complete the Application for Enterprise Registration (Form II.1) electronically, attaching the scanned Investment Registration Certificate, the Member-approved Charter, the members' quota list, the legal-representative's identification, and the office lease with notarized landlord consent. The system validates enterprise name uniqueness and the lawfulness of the object clauses. The DPI issues the Certificate of Enterprise Registration within three working days; the certificate simultaneously generates the Enterprise Code and Tax Identification Number and evidences the Company's legal personality. No minimum capital verification is required at this stage, but the declared charter capital schedule is integrated into the DICA monitoring framework.
required_dossiers: Issued Investment Registration Certificate
Signed and scanned Form II.1 Enterprise Registration Application
Charter adopted by the Members' Council, notarized
List of founding members and their subscribed capital quotas
Office lease agreement plus notarized landlord's consent
Vietnamese ID / passport of the legal representative and appointment resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DPI interfaces a data mismatch, rectify the inconsistent field and resubmit through the portal; if the Charter's language is non-compliant with Form Charter provisions of Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP, the file will adopt the requested mandatory clauses and the applicant may re-file the conformed charter within the statutory response period; an unjustified refusal beyond the deadline may be challenged before the Minister of Planning and Investment and the competent administrative court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Seal Physicalization, Seal Imprint Notification and National Portal Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company in its autonomous seal-management capacity; Business Registration Office for seal-imprint notification; National Business Registration Portal publication module (dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn) as the official gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the CER is granted, the General Director executes the company's internal seal-control policy approving the seal material, design, custody, and strict usage authorization, then arranges the physical creation of the corporate seal at a private seal-engraving vendor licensed under the relevant resolution of the Government. The Company files the seal imprint notification with the Business Registration Office in the statutorily prescribed manner so that the seal impression is recorded in the National Enterprise Information System. The Company likewise causes the enterprise registration information to be published on the National Business Registration Portal, including the legal representative, charter capital, forms of paying-in capital, and business lines, satisfying the publication obligation of Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Enterprise Registration
Internal seal control resolution and custody policy
Seal imprint notification form filed online
Payment record for portal publication fee (VND 300,000 equivalent)
Power of attorney for the publication filing agent, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the seal notification is not reflected on the system within the statutory period, file a corrected notification via the Portal assistance desk; if the publication posting fails or contains errors, contact the National Business Registration Portal helpdesk to cure with a corrected certified extract and republish without any fee duplication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: DICA Bank Account Opening, Charter Capital Contribution, Tax Licence-Fee Registration and Social Insurance Enrolments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank in Viet Nam (DICA-approved branch); provincial General Department of Taxation through the electronic tax filing portal (thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn); provincial Social Insurance Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the Direct Investment Capital Account at the chosen custodian bank, submitting the CER, IRC, Charter, board signatory letter, and AML KYC disclosures. Transfer the subscribed charter capital in cash into the DICA within 90 days from CER issuance; the bank is legally obliged to report capital-contribution shortfalls to the DPI. Register the Company with the tax authority for licence fee (monetary licence duty / le phi mon bai), noting that a newly founded LLC is exempt in its first operating year and thereafter pays VND 3,000,000 per annum for charter capital above VND 2 billion. Complete the electronic tax registration for the Corporate Income Tax, Value Added Tax on advisory fees, and Final Withholding Tax on cross-border payments, obtain the e-tax authentication token for the legal representative, and enrol the Company as an employer with the provincial Social Insurance Agency for compulsory health, social, and unemployment insurance of all employees. File the initial labour-usage schedule and, given the AML risk profile, file the regulatory notice of reporting-entity status under Law No. 04/2024/QH15.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Enterprise Registration and Investment Registration Certificate
Charter and board resolution naming bank signatories
Documentary evidence of capital transfer instructions into DICA
Monetary licence-fee declaration form 01/LPMB
Tax registration questionnaire and legal representative's identification
Labour contract templates and social insurance employer registration form
AML reporting-entity notice with nominated compliance officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises enhanced KYC questions on the M&A fee model, supplement with the documented ownership chain and engagement-letter sample; if the tax authority requires additional notarized exemplars on the licence-fee declaration, cure within 10 working days; if the 90-day capital-contribution deadline is missed, the General Director must submit a formal explanation to the DPI and remedy the shortfall promptly, otherwise the Company may be subject to a forced dissolution procedure under Article 75 of the Law on Enterprises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical Premises and Workplace Clearance: Fire Safety, Structural-Occupancy and Environmental Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Fire Prevention, Fighting and Rescue Police Department under the Ministry of Public Security; provincial construction and civil-defense inspectorate; Environmental Registry of the provincial Department of Natural Resources and Environment (DONRE) or the commune-level People's Committee where registration is applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the boutique leases space in a class II or III commercial building, obtain from the lessor the building-wide fire-safety acceptance certificate and the fire-alarm and suppression maintenance records applicable to the leased floor; arrange a licensed inspector to verify evacuation pathways, exit signage, fire extinguishers, and emergency lighting. If the Company operates a standalone ground-floor office meeting the floor-area thresholds of Decree No. 136/2020/ND-CP, apply for the statutory Certificate of Fire Safety Eligibility before full operation. Conduct an occupational safety and health workplace risk assessment as required by the Law on Occupational Safety and Health No. 84/2015/QH13, including electrical, workstation ergonomics, lighting, and noise parameters. For environmental compliance, determine whether the building aggregated domestic-wastewater volume exceeds 10 m3/day applicable to the boutique; if so, file an Environmental Registration with the competent body, and in any event execute a waste-segregation and municipal-collection arrangement, maintain a hazardous-waste registry for toner and e-waste, and keep the required records for the annual environmental report under Decree No. 08/2022/ND-CP.
required_dossiers: Lessor's building fire-safety acceptance certificate and maintenance log
Certificate of Fire Safety Eligibility application (if standalone category triggers)
Occupational health and safety risk assessment and employee-training log
Environmental registration form for office/commercial operation, if threshold triggered
Solid-waste collection agreement and hazardous-waste designation list
Structural load and occupancy certificate of the leased floor for office use
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If fire-safety inspection identifies deficiencies, remediate the listed items (exits, extinguishers, signage, compartmentation) and request a re-inspection before commencing operations; if the DONRE queries the environmental registration, supplement with floor-level wastewater flow certificates and amend the registration; refusal of the occupancy certificate is cured by retrofitting and obtaining an architect's structural compliance statement under QCVN standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Primary licensing authority: Business Registration Office of the provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) issuing the Investment Registration Certificate and Certificate of Enterprise Registration. Conditional secondary licensing authority where the M&A boutique extends to securities-linked advisory in Viet Nam: State Securities Commission (SSC) of the Ministry of Finance under Law on Securities No. 54/2019/QH14. Physical premises authority: Fire Prevention, Fighting and Rescue Police Department under the Ministry of Public Security; environmental registry under the provincial Department of Natural Resources and Environment (DONRE) or the relevant commune-level People's Committee.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Primary statutory operating licences for the ISIC 7020 advisory-only boutique: Investment Registration Certificate (Giay chung nhan dang ky dau tu) and Certificate of Enterprise Registration (Giay chung nhan dang ky doanh nghiep), which together constitute the valid commercial licence for non-conditional M&A advisory services. Conditional secondary licence where the boutique delivers securities-advice in Vietnam: 'Certificate of Eligibility for Provision of Securities Advisory Services' (Giay chung nhan du dieu kien cung cap dich vu tu van ve chung khoan) issued by the State Securities Commission, together with the issuer-side individual securities-practice certificates for advising analysts.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MONRE) for general policy and guidance; provincial Department of Natural Resources and Environment (DONRE) and commune-level People's Committee for the specific registration and inspection of office operations under Law on Environmental Protection No. 72/2020/QH14 and Decree No. 08/2022/ND-CP
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full EIA Report: NOT REQUIRED because an M&A advisory boutique is a genuine office operation and does not fall within Appendix II of Decree No. 08/2022/ND-CP. Classification tier: REGISTRATION-EXEMPT at the standard boutique scale (less than 10 m3/day domestic wastewater). If the building-wide discharge or the Company's leased floor operates above 10 m3/day of domestic wastewater, an Environmental Registration (Dang ky moi truong) is required at the commune-level People's Committee; a Simplified Environmental Permit (Giay phep moi truong) is required only where the aggregated discharge exceeds 100 m3/day, which is non-applicable for a consulting office. The boutique must in all cases maintain waste segregation and hazardous-waste handling records under Circular No. 02/2022/TT-BTNMT.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Domestic wastewater discharged to the municipal sewer must meet QCVN 14:2008/BTNMT, Column B (BOD5 max 50 mg/L; TSS max 100 mg/L; total coliforms max 5,000 MPN/100 mL), as incorporated into the lessor building's sewer-discharge permit. Office airborne emissions from printers and HVAC systems must satisfy ambient indoor-air thresholds under QCVN 06:2021/BTNMT and occupational exposure limits of Circular No. 24/2020/TT-BYT (formaldehyde, total volatile organic compounds, and particulate matter within recommended office workplace limits). Hazardous wastes (toner cartridges, batteries, electronic equipment) must be stored in labelled leak-proof containers, declared, and transferred exclusively to a licensed hazardous-waste transporter; e-waste may not be mixed with municipal solid waste. Municipal solid waste must be segregated at source under municipal waste-collection regulations and delivered to the local service provider.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under Decree No. 136/2020/ND-CP: for a leased class II or III commercial office, the lessor's fire-acceptance certificate and full building PCCC maintenance records must cover the boutique's floor; the boutique itself must undergo inspection of fire extinguishers, automatic alarm points, evacuation directional signage, emergency exit capacity, and employee fire-warden training. A standalone boutique with net floor area exceeding the Decree thresholds requires the Certificate of Eligibility for Fire Prevention and Fighting issued by the provincial Fire Police before personnel occupancy. Structural-load and safe-escape clearance is evidenced by the building's occupancy certificate under QCVN 03:2009/BXD, the Law on Fire Prevention and Fighting No. 27/2001/QH10 (as amended by Law No. 40/2013/QH12), and the Law on Civil Defense No. 23/2023/QH16 (effective 1 July 2024). Occupational workplace clearance under the Law on Occupational Safety and Health No. 84/2015/QH13 requires a documented workplace risk assessment covering fire drills, electrical safety, workstation ergonomics per TCVN 7114:2002, first-aid equipment, and pre-employment and annual medical examinations for all employees; the General Director must carry the labour-safety statement and training records at the registered office for inspection by the provincial labour inspectorate.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: General Department of Taxation (Tổng cục Thuế), Ministry of Finance of the Socialist Republic of Viet Nam; Electronic tax filing portal: etaxvn.gdt.gov.vn; National e-invoice clearance and registration portal: hoadon.dichvucong.gov.vn
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Obtain the Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) from the provincial Department of Planning and Investment or through the National Foreign Investment Portal (dautugocp.gov.vn) for the licensed foreign-invested enterprise. Step 2: Obtain the Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC); the tax identification number (Mã số thuế - MST) is automatically and concurrently granted upon ERC issuance, so no separate TIN application is required for the domestic LLC. Step 3: File Supplementary Tax Registration Information (Form 05-ĐK-TCT) with the local tax authority, including the election of the VAT calculation method (credit method) and e-invoice registration. Step 4: Register an official digital signature (USB token/e-signature) and activate the eTax account on etaxvn.gdt.gov.vn. Step 5: For non-resident advisors without a permanent establishment, a separate foreign-person TIN is obtained through the withholding agent (Form 01-ĐK-TCT) for Foreign Contractor Tax purposes, but this does not alter the LLC's own Vietnamese TIN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the Foreign-Invested LLC is a Viet Nam tax resident taxed at the 20% standard CIT rate on worldwide income; there is no pass-through eligibility and no tax-exempt zone status in the ordinary course; Territorial_Scope is global for resident LLCs, with offshore passive income subject to attribution and controlled-foreign-company type rules under Vietnamese tax administration and transfer-pricing frameworks.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Viet Nam does not operate a check-the-box election or OECD hybrid-mismatch election regime. Available statutory elections: (i) mandatory VAT credit method for companies with annual turnover above VND 1 billion; (ii) optional direct method on value-added for taxpayers below the statutory turnover ceiling; (iii) election to apply CIT incentive schedules (e.g., 10% preferential rate, tax holidays and reductions) for qualifying investment projects by sector and location; (iv) election to enter into Advance Pricing Agreements (APA) with the General Department of Taxation under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP; (v) election of quarterly vs monthly tax filing for CIT/VAT; (vi) no entity-level hybrid-mismatch elections — intra-group financing, royalties and management fees are instead constrained by thin-capitalization and related-party transaction rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for corporate entities: all LLCs must register for VAT upon enterprise registration. Only non-corporate household and individual business activities with annual taxable turnover not exceeding VND 100,000,000 are outside the VAT net; an LLC operating as an M&A Advisory Boutique has an unconditional VAT registration obligation regardless of expected turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing has applied to all enterprises since 1 July 2022 under Decree 123/2020/ND-CP and Circular 78/2021/TT-BTC. Invoices with tax-authority codes must be cleared in real time through the national portal hoadon.dichvucong.gov.vn before issuance; the enterprise transmits digitally signed XML/SOAP messages to the tax authority's infrastructure through certified e-invoice service providers (TMS API integration). Self-issued e-invoices without tax-authority codes must be transferred to the tax authority within one working day of issuance. Every e-invoice requires a Vietnamese digital signature token and a QR code for fiscal authentication; failure to clear electronically renders the invoice invalid for input VAT credits and for export zero-rating claims.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A zero-rated (0%) VAT supply is available for cross-border services, including M&A advisory services, only where all conditions of Article 9 of the Law on VAT (No. 13/2008/QH12 as amended), Decree 219/2013/ND-CP and Circular 72/2013/TT-BTC are met: (i) the advisory service is provided to a foreign customer (an organization or individual resident abroad) or to an export-processing entity; (ii) the service is actually consumed outside Viet Nam (advisory deliverables, offshore decision-making and closing activities occurring abroad); (iii) there is a signed service contract documenting the foreign recipient and place of performance; (iv) payment is received from abroad in a convertible foreign currency through an authorized Vietnamese bank; and (v) the enterprise holds complete accounting vouchers proving the offshore supply. Services rendered to onshore parties or consumed in Viet Nam are not zero-rated and remain subject to output VAT at 10%; failure to satisfy any condition transmutes the supply into a domestic taxable service.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (required only for embedded physical deliverables/goods; a pure advisory service does not generate a customs declaration)
Export Service Contract / engagement letter identifying the offshore client, scope of work, and place of consumption
Zero-rated VAT e-Invoice with tax-authority code issued and cleared under Decree 123/2020/ND-CP
Inward Remittance Certificate (Giấy báo Có) or foreign-currency bank statement evidencing that the success fee was remitted from abroad
Statement of Work, time sheets, closing schedules and delivery memos evidencing performance and consumption outside Viet Nam
Retained correspondence and deal documentation substantiating offshore consumption (retention period: 10 years under Vietnamese tax record-keeping rules)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The General Department of Taxation scrutinizes export zero-rating claims through dedicated desks and post-refund audits. Where a zero-rating claim is found fraudulent: the VAT refund is clawed back retrospectively, the 0% rate is re-characterized as 10% output VAT, and the enterprise is liable for the full underdeclared output VAT plus late-payment interest at 0.03% per day and penalties under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP ranging from 1 to 3 times the evaded tax for material VAT misdeclaration, and up to 20%-50% of the tax plus administrative fines for erroneous declarations. For criminal tax evasion under Article 200 of the Penal Code, penalties include fines up to VND 4.5 billion and imprisonment up to 7 years. The tax-administration limitation period for fraud cases is 10 years, during which the General Department of Taxation may reopen returns, disallow all related input credits, sanction responsible tax practitioners, and blacklist the entity for future VAT refund clearances.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Bank of Vietnam (Ngân hàng Nhà nước Việt Nam, SBV) — the Republic of Viet Nam's sole central bank and foreign exchange administration. SBV operates under the Law on the State Bank of Vietnam 2010, the Law on Credit Institutions 2024, and the Ordinance on Foreign Exchange 2005, as amended by Law No. 75/2019/QH14. The SBV sets the daily central reference rate for VND, administers the permitted intraday VND/USD trading band, issues all FX-management decrees and circulars (including Circular 15/2015/TT-NHNN on FX activities of credit institutions and Circular 05/2021/TT-NHNN on foreign exchange management for foreign direct investment), and chairs national Balance of Payments and monetary stabilization policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: VND operates under a managed floating exchange-rate regime with limited, condition-based convertibility. Current-account transactions — including cross-border advisory service fees, success fees, interest, royalties, and after-tax profit remittances — are freely convertible through SBV-licensed intermediaries without prior SBV licensing approval, subject to underlying documentation, tax clearance, and bank-level due diligence. The capital account remains restricted: all foreign direct investment equity inflows must enter through a registered Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA); external commercial borrowings require a Foreign Loan Registration Certificate; outbound investments and capital repatriation require investment licence backing; and derivative transactions must be executed with SBV-licensed banks in respect of a verified real commercial exposure. For the M&A advisory boutique, foreign-currency success fees earned from offshore clients are characterized as service-export receipts enjoying current-account convertibility, but profit distribution to the foreign shareholder remains a capital-account operation and must satisfy cumulative conditions: (i) audited annual financial statements filed, (ii) full payment of corporate income tax and any Foreign Contractor Tax obligations, (iii) prior-year accumulated losses fully absorbed, and (iv) lodgement of a profit-remittance declaration and supporting tax certificates with the DICA-holding bank. No quantitative annual remittance cap is imposed on compliant after-tax profits, though banks apply strict documentary scrutiny and report all remittances to SBV in the periodic FX statistics return.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Circular 15/2015/TT-NHNN, as amended, all export proceeds — including cross-border service fees and success fees invoiced by the M&A advisory boutique to non-resident clients — must be repatriated to a foreign-currency account held at an SBV-licensed commercial bank within 90 calendar days from the date of service completion or the contractual payment due date, whichever is later; an extension of up to 180 days may be granted by the bank on documented cash-flow justifications. Mandatory statutory conversion ratios for export receipts were definitively abolished in 2012; the current surrender ratio is 0%, meaning exporters are not required to convert foreign-currency receipts into VND and may retain and redeploy foreign currency through their licensed foreign-currency accounts. However, SBV reserves a residual power, in extraordinary balance-of-payments stress, to issue temporary administrative directives requiring selected exporters to convert a stated percentage of their foreign-currency balances; banks will then enforce such directive. The 90-day repatriation window is a hard compliance point for the boutique's offshore fee collections, and failure to repatriate exposes the entity to administrative sanctions under the FX-control legal framework.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-conditional viability rating. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Revolut Business, Currencycloud) do not hold a direct licensing standing under the Law on Credit Institutions 2024 and Decree 101/2012/ND-CP on non-cash payments. Such EMIs are not permitted to open VND-denominated domestic payment accounts, issue local payment cards, or execute domestic payment instructions in Viet Nam without an SBV intermediary license or a licensed technical-background agreement with a Vietnamese bank. For the M&A boutique, an offshore EMI may lawfully be used as an auxiliary collection conduit for non-resident clients under an offshore service agreement, provided all proceeds are swept and repatriated to the Vietnamese DICA/operating account within the 90-day statutory window and are fully traceable to identified underlying engagements. The EMI route must be disclosed to the Vietnamese settlement bank to avoid unexplained-third-party-credit flags, and must never be used for local operating disbursements, escrow, or tax payments, which require SBV-licensed banking rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for corporate account opening. For a foreign-invested medium-risk M&A advisory LLC, Vietnamese Tier-1 banks require at least the legal representative (General Director) and, in practice, one additional authorized signatory — both bearing original government-issued identification — to appear in-person at a designated branch for the initial KYC interview. Where the General Director is non-resident, a physically present Vietnamese-resident authorized signatory holding a notarized and consularized power of attorney may substitute for signing, but the ultimate beneficial owners still must be identified through documentary evidence and, where requested, a remote videoconference interview. Pure remote/digital corporate onboarding is not accepted by major Vietnamese banks for foreign-invested entities, notwithstanding the availability of supplementary e-KYC for individual low-risk accounts. The bank will capture original Enterprise Registration Certificate, Investment Registration Certificate, company seal, specimen signatures, UBO declarations, and relevant financial statements; the interview includes an oral explanation of the expected transaction profile, source of wealth, and purpose of the account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO concentration domiciled in a high-risk or secrecy jurisdiction (e.g., Cayman Islands, BVI SPV shareholders) creating opacity as to ultimate natural-person control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed SBV-compliant UBO declaration form; full corporate chain chart tracing every intermediate entity to natural persons; certified copies of passports and proof of residence for each natural-person UBO; apostilled or consularized certificate of incorporation, register of directors, register of shareholders, and beneficial ownership register of each holding entity; sworn source-of-wealth and source-of-charter-capital affidavit; reference letters from the foreign shareholder's home bank confirming account conduct; and evidence of economic substance (premises, staff, financial statements) of the SPV in its domicile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared business profile (M&A advisory boutique) and expected flows — high-value success fees from unrelated counterparties without commensurate local operational substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed engagement letters and M&A advisory agreements for the prior and current years; itemized success-fee invoices aligned with deal milestone documents; signed closing certificates and deal-completion memoranda; board resolutions approving invoicing and collection; client-side payment confirmations; corporate income tax declarations and VAT filings evidencing declared service turnover; local substance documentation including office lease, payroll records, social insurance filings, and staff list.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments routed through multiple third-country intermediary hubs (e.g., Singapore, Hong Kong SAR) or a third-party payor paying on behalf of the contractual client, which triggers unexplained-credit and layering alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full contractual chain demonstrating the identity of the contractual payor; legally executed third-party payment authorization or side letter from the account party to the boutique; declaration of final beneficiary and economic purpose of the payment; the client's bank reference confirming that the third-party payor has authorization; the underlying transaction flow chart and closing statement; and, where the payor is an affiliate, transfer-pricing documentation in accordance with Ministry of Finance regulations and the OECD-aligned guidance applied in Viet Nam.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) identified among target-company shareholders or counterparties in the boutique's M&A transactions, creating reputational and corruption-risk exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date PEP screening reports generated at onboarding and refreshed at each significant transaction; independent adverse-media and sanctions searches against all target shareholders; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth declarations for PEP-linked counterparties; an institutional enhanced-due-diligence memorandum prepared in-house and presented to the bank; enforcement of an internal PEP threshold policy; and written confirmation from the Directors that no sanctioned or prohibited person is a beneficial recipient of the transaction proceeds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicious transaction-pattern indicators — large cash withdrawals, repeated same-day round-trip wires, or crypto-currency-linked references on SWIFT instructions inconsistent with professional advisory service.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Adopted written treasury and anti-money-laundering policy expressly prohibiting cash settlements and crypto-linked payment references; complete bank statements and wire confirmation archive showing the benign purpose of each transaction; standard client-vetting procedure manuals and training records for compliance staff; a strict SWIFT reference-field tagging policy that restricts remittance information to invoice, contract, and deal code only; and a documented audit trail of the bank's requested transaction-level explanations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injection for the foreign-invested LLC follows a strict gatekeeping protocol. Step 1: the foreign investor contributes charter capital strictly in accordance with the contribution schedule recorded in the Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) and Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC) issued by the provincial Investment Registration Authority. Step 2: the company opens a Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) at an SBV-licensed commercial bank in accordance with Circular 05/2021/TT-NHNN; this account is the exclusive gateway for all cash equity injections and subsequent capital repatriation. Step 3: the investor executes each inbound transfer via SWIFT MT103 or MT202, referencing the DICA account number, the exact investor legal name, the IRC/ERC certificate numbers, and the standard purpose code for direct investment capital contribution; the remitter bank must show the funds originating from the registered foreign investor's own account, not from an unrelated third party. Step 4: the receiving Vietnamese bank verifies the remitter against the IRC/ERC, screens the wire for sanctions/AML, confirms the source of funds, and then converts the foreign currency into VND at the bank's posted rate with respect to the SBV's daily reference rate and trading band, crediting the DICA or a linked operational VND account. Step 5: the bank issues a capital-contribution confirmation / DICA transaction statement, which serves as evidence for the later registration of paid-in capital, profit remittance calculations, and potential future capital divestment. Any foreign-loan component (e.g., shareholder loan or international facility) cannot be routed through the DICA; it requires a separate Foreign Loan Registration Certificate and a dedicated loan-drawdown account with the same licensed bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements from the M&A advisory boutique utilize licensed clearing rails with full bank supervision. For operational and sub-advisory payments to non-resident service providers (overseas financial advisors, law firms, due-diligence providers, and data-room vendors), the primary rail is SWIFT MT103 executed after the bank verifies the underlying contract, invoice, Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT) withholding status, and value-added tax evidence; the bank will reference purpose codes consistent with service-import classification. For settlement of transaction-related escrow flows and closing payments under the boutique's intermediation, the permitted rails are SWIFT MT103/MT202 in combination with the licensed bank's escrow account mechanism; commercial letters of credit are structurally inapplicable to advisory fee disbursements and are reserved for trade-in-goods settlements, which the boutique will not initiate. For profit distribution to foreign shareholders, the boutique must apply through the DICA-holding bank, presenting (i) the annual audited financial statements, (ii) the corporate income tax finalization certificate, (iii) a board resolution declaring the dividend, and (iv) a profit-remittance declaration confirming that all accumulated losses and statutory reserves have been settled; the bank will then remit via SWIFT MT103 tagged with the dividend/profit-remittance purpose code and will report the transaction within the statutory SBV periodic return. All outbound transfers slightly above the SBV-prescribed reporting threshold are automatically captured in the bank's transaction monitoring and transmitted to SBV; absent complete documentation the bank is legally entitled to refuse execution.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forwards between VND and USD/EUR for hedging the boutique's foreign-currency fee receivables and committed payables, executed with SBV-licensed banks within the authorized maximum tenor (commonly up to 365 days) and subject to documentary proof of the underlying commercial exposure.

FX swaps (spot-versus-forward and forward-versus-forward) combining simultaneous spot and forward VND/USD legs for managing short-term liquidity positions and rolling trade-related exposures with licensed banks.

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CIRS) between VND-linked liabilities and USD obligations, permitted where the boutique carries qualifying FDI debt or investment-related exposure and the bank confirms the hedge relationship.

European-style currency options — including plain-vanilla VND/USD calls and puts — offered by SBV-licensed credit institutions under the FX derivatives regulatory framework, used to cap downside conversion risk on success-fee receivables while preserving upside participation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) via National Enterprise Registration Information System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March (within 90 days of the fiscal year-end 31 December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of VND 10,000,000-20,000,000 (approx. USD 400-800) for late filing; VND 20,000,000-30,000,000 for false declarations; persistent non-compliance may trigger enterprise registration suspension and compulsory strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 January; newly incorporated enterprises are exempt for the first calendar year of operation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 0.03% per day; administrative fines up to VND 20,000,000 (approx. USD 800) for non-payment; enforced collection and tax debt summons.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) and Provincial Tax Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March; audit must be completed and audited financial statements attached to the annual tax finalization and annual enterprise report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to VND 20,000,000 (approx. USD 800) for failure to submit audited financial statements; director-level sanctions; loss of investment incentives and enhanced risk of tax reassessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Finalization Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Department of Taxation (GDT) / Provincial Tax Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March (90th day from the fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 0.03% per day; late-return fines ranging VND 1,500,000-25,000,000 (approx. USD 65-1,100); underpayment penalties of 20%-75% of additional tax; bank account freezes and asset seizure in serious cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: State Securities Commission Annual Compliance Report (M&A Advisory License)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Securities Commission (SSC), Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 60 days from the fiscal year-end if the company holds an M&A advisory license issued by the SSC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Warning, license suspension or revocation; administrative fines under the Law on Securities 2019; personal liability of compliance officers and chief executives for misstatement.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All foreign-invested enterprises, including 100% foreign-owned LLCs, must undergo an independent annual audit regardless of revenue or asset size. Domestic LLCs are also required to be audited if they meet prescribed thresholds (e.g., annual revenue above VND 10 billion or total assets above VND 5 billion) under Decree 174/2016/ND-CP.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Vietnam Accounting Standards (VAS); IFRS may be applied voluntarily by eligible enterprises for consolidation and internal reporting, but statutory financial statements are prepared under VAS-based accounting regime.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Enterprise Law 2020 and Anti-Money Laundering Law 2022, the LLC must maintain an up-to-date member and ultimate beneficial owner register. Any change in shareholding or beneficial ownership must be reported to the Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) within 30 days. No separate annual UBO declaration is required; however, the annual enterprise report confirms the current member/UBO list and must be certified by the legal representative.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (Members' Council, Chairman, and General Director)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard 20% applies to a middle-market M&A advisory boutique unless it qualifies for an investment incentive under the Law on Corporate Income Tax (No. 14/2008/QH12 as amended): 10% rate for 15 years and 2-year CIT exemption plus 50% reduction for up to 4–9 years (for projects in high-tech zones, hi-tech parks, supporting industries, or new investment in areas with extremely difficult socio-economic conditions). Service enterprises outside encouraged sectors generally receive no rate holiday. Small and micro enterprises may apply the reduced SME rate schedule (20% standard; micro-enterprises may access the simplified regime).
